newsitem.title: UK: British-Borneo unsurprised by share rise.
newsitem.headline: British-Borneo unsurprised by share rise.

text.p: British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc said on Thursday it was unsurprised by the recent strong gains in its shares, but added it was not approached by any party that might consider launching a takeover bid.
Finance director Bill Colvin also told Reuters he ruled out a rights issue to help finance the $210 million development of the Morpeth field in the Gulf of Mexico.
Colvin said he saw few risks for a successful development of the deep sea oil and gas field.
British Borneo shares were 52 pence higher at 990 pence by 1254 GMT after having already powered ahead uninteruptedly from a closing level of 789 pence on Friday.
Commenting on the share price, Colvin said: "I am not surprised. Asset value has increased significantly and there is good exploration potential."

He noted the oil exploration and production sector was rife with bid talk following Gulf Canada's offer for Clyde Petroleum late in December, but he added he was unaware of specific any bidding interest for British Borneo.
